projects.name: WGS Extract
projects.progress: Releasing regularly (v0.8.x). The desktop app is in alpha, and Linux ARM64 support is in phase 1.
projects.summary: A local-first toolkit that turns whole-genome sequencing files into useful files, reports and extracts, as a scriptable CLI plus a desktop app.
highlights: An independent command-line rewrite of WGS Extract that wraps samtools, bcftools, bwa/minimap2, GATK, Haplogrep and VEP
Inspects BAM/CRAM files, simulates consumer microarray files (23andMe, AncestryDNA), and calls and annotates variants
Includes native Yleaf-derived Y-DNA haplogroup analysis
Ships a cross-platform desktop app (Tauri) built with GUI for CLI, plus one-line installers
Built to be AI-agent friendly: everything is a CLI command with structured output

projects.name: GUI for CLI
projects.progress: The framework and the WGS Extract app now live inside wgsextract-cli/gui. This repository keeps the history, including a dozen experimental renderers.
projects.summary: Turns a portable CLI-tool bundle (a manifest plus pages) into an installable desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux.
highlights: One TypeScript app: a web UI and a local Node backend, packaged as a native app with Tauri
Data-driven pages: setup steps, long-running commands, dynamic data sources, localization, file pickers and terminal output
Explored a dozen desktop frameworks first (SwiftUI, Electron and more) and benchmarked them before settling on Tauri
Over 600 commits and 22 releases before it was folded into WGS Extract

screenshots.caption: Running the WGS Extract example bundle

projects.name: The Dawn-Breakers
projects.progress: A playable, non-combat prototype with about ten chapters, mini-games, journeys, a map editor, and English, Persian and Chinese text.
projects.summary: A 2.5D isometric web RPG inspired by Nabíl's narrative The Dawn-Breakers. You explore historical places, talk to people and follow the story chapter by chapter.
highlights: Isometric exploration, reflective dialogue, journals and chapter progression
Historical set pieces from Karbilá, Shíráz, Iṣfahán, Baghdád and the mountain prisons
Animated sunrise title screen with its own soundtrack
Most of the code, art, music, writing and translation was made with AI, and the game says so

screenshots.caption: Karbilá: the palm groves on the canal

projects.name: Amaran Light CLI
projects.progress: Published on npm as amaran-light-cli with 25 releases. It runs my desk lights every day.
projects.summary: Command-line control for Aputure Amaran lights through Amaran Desktop or directly over Bluetooth Mesh, with circadian lighting that follows the sun.
highlights: auto-cct sets colour temperature and brightness from the sun's position at your location
A background service applies it every minute; weather-aware adjustments
A local BLE Mesh daemon, so the vendor app is optional
Presets, scenes, groups, effects, fan profiles and thermal telemetry

projects.name: Reddit ZST to Parquet
projects.progress: Converted my full multi-terabyte Reddit archive (comments and submissions up to 2026-03). It still has rough edges.
projects.summary: Converts huge Reddit Zstandard dumps into analytical Parquet files, using several machines that coordinate through your NAS.
highlights: Distributed by design: workers on different machines claim work through a ticket system on shared storage
Tunes DuckDB memory and threads to each machine
Resilient transfers over FTP/FTPS, rsync/SSH, NFS or local disks
Writes a JSON manifest with row counts and column stats for every Parquet file

projects.name: Email Sorter
projects.progress: Used on my own gigabytes of mail. You bring your own local LLM server.
projects.summary: An offline email classification pipeline that sorts gigabytes of mail with heuristics and local language models, spread across several LLM machines.
highlights: Ingests Google Takeout mbox files or Fastmail through JMAP
Runs fast heuristics and language detection first, then sends the rest to an LLM
Works with any OpenAI-compatible server (LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM), and with several machines at once
Exports ban and unsubscribe lists, with a browser-based unsubscribe fallback

projects.name: AI Node Management
projects.progress: Used to provision my own Linux and Windows AI machines.
projects.summary: Builds reproducible, unattended USB installers for remotely managed Linux and Windows AI nodes, with an optional Orca appliance reachable only over Tailscale.
highlights: Unattended Ubuntu Server 24.04 and Windows 11 Pro installers with safe automatic disk selection
Wi-Fi, Tailscale, SSH, recovery access and a console health display ready on first boot
A Docker Compose Orca appliance published only on the host's Tailscale address
A cross-platform hardware and agent-tool inventory dashboard generator

projects.name: FFMI Calculator
projects.progress: Live on GitHub Pages.
projects.summary: A calculator for FFMI, weight and body fat, with muscle-gain projections and dynamic fat-loss timelines.
highlights: Linked FFMI, weight and body-fat inputs: change one and the others follow
Fat-loss timelines limited by how fast stored fat can be used, with optional uncertainty bands
Population defaults for 190 regions; metric, imperial and stone/pound units
Shareable URLs, plus a terminal CLI that uses the same calculation code

projects.name: Exercise Video Annotator
projects.progress: Works on my own multi-camera workout recordings, and everything runs locally.
projects.summary: Finds and labels exercise sets in workout videos with local vision models and pose tracking, then lets you review them on a multi-camera timeline.
highlights: Finds exercise intervals with X-CLIP or a local vision-language model
Uses MediaPipe pose motion and repetition evidence to refine the boundaries
Synchronized multi-camera review UI for turning proposals into ground truth
Accuracy evaluation and a personal classifier trained on your own clips

screenshots.caption: Multi-camera pose review (video hidden for privacy)

projects.name: skill-dump
projects.progress: Installed on all my machines; updates on every git pull.
projects.summary: My AI-agent skills, plus the command-line tools my agents use on every computer, installed by one command.

Links skills into Claude, Codex, Copilot and other agents' skill folders
Tools for agent coordination, audited sudo and 1Password sessions, and more
Can also be installed from agent skill marketplaces

projects.name: Sheprd (formerly Herdr UI)
projects.progress: 17 merged pull requests so far.

Shared one SSH login per host for the app's short commands
Open remote folders in VS Code, reopen closed tabs, and move tabs between workspaces
